accessibility.title: Accessibility statement
accessibility.subtitle: What is accessible, what is not yet, and who to contact
accessibility.intro: We treat accessibility as part of the craft rather than an addition to it. This system is built so that everyone working in the clinic can use it — with a mouse, with a keyboard alone, or with a screen reader.
accessibility.standard: The system is built to Israeli standard 5568, which follows WCAG 2.1 level AA. This statement is updated as the work continues.

done.keyboard: Full keyboard navigation on every screen — menus, filters, table sorting and the acupuncture point chart included — with a visible focus indicator throughout.
done.contrast: Every colour pair that carries text is measured automatically against the 4.5:1 requirement. The check runs on the built code and fails if a new pair falls below the threshold.
done.landmarks: Semantic HTML: a correct heading hierarchy, navigation, main content and header marked as such, and a skip-to-content link at the top of every page.
done.labels: Every form field has an associated label, and every error message is linked to its field and announced — not signalled by colour alone.
done.rtl: Full right-to-left Hebrew support, including menus, tables and dialogs mirroring correctly, while phone numbers and Latin codes keep their own direction.
done.zoom: The layout is built in relative units and stays usable at 200% text zoom.
done.motion: No flashing animation, nothing that moves on its own, and no time limit on completing a form.
done.automated: Automated checks run on every code change: contrast is measured from the stylesheet across 101 pairs, and axe checks labels, accessible names, heading order and direction.

accessibility.gapsIntro: This list is deliberately specific. A statement that claims full conformance and is wrong is worse than one that names its own limits.

gaps.screenReaderAudit: A full manual pass with a screen reader (NVDA or VoiceOver) has not been done yet. Fixes so far were driven by the code and by automated checks.
gaps.bodyMap: The acupuncture body chart is shown both as a 3D model and as a flat drawing. The 3D model is an image only; every point marked on it also appears as a keyboard-accessible button beneath it, and in the point list beside it.
gaps.calendar: The calendar view has not had a full accessibility pass. Every appointment is also reachable from the patient file.
gaps.pdf: Uploaded documents are shown as they arrive. If a document we receive is not accessible, we cannot make it so after the fact.
gaps.automatedScope: The automated axe check currently covers the public pages only. The screens behind the login need a test environment with synthetic data, which is not yet in place.

accessibility.contactBody: If something stops you using the system, we want to hear about it and will act on it. Accessibility reports are handled as a priority.
accessibility.placeholderWarning: The accessibility coordinator has not been named. Before this system serves patients, a name, email address and phone number must be entered here — a statement with no way to make contact does not meet the standard.

feed.regenerateBody: The old address stops working, and Google and the iPhone need subscribing again with the new one.

google.title: Instructions for Google Calendar
google.step1: On a computer, in Google Calendar: next to "Other calendars" click + and then "From URL".
google.step2: Paste the address above and click "Add calendar".
google.step3: The calendar also appears in the Google app on your phone, under the same account.
google.note: Google refreshes a URL calendar every few hours — a booking made now shows up there a little later.

iphone.title: Instructions for iPhone
iphone.step1: Settings → Apps → Calendar → Accounts → Add Account → Other → Add Subscribed Calendar.
iphone.step3: The calendar appears in the iPhone's Calendar app, and you can give it a colour.
iphone.note: The iPhone refreshes on its own schedule — in the calendar settings you can choose "Every hour".

schedule.title: Working hours
schedule.subtitle: The days and hours you see patients, and diary closures. Other hours are shaded in the calendar, not blocked.
schedule.hoursSaveFailed: Could not save the working hours. Please try again.
schedule.closuresHint: A holiday, a festival, a course. One day or a range of dates.
schedule.closureSaveFailed: Could not close the diary. Please try again.

protocols.title: Treatment protocols
protocols.subtitle: Point and prescription combinations you return to. A protocol fills the treatment in and leaves everything open to edit.
protocols.saveFromTreatmentHint: Saves this treatment’s points and prescription for reuse
protocols.saveFromTreatmentBody: Saves the points, the treatment principle and the latest prescription from this treatment — as they are stored, not as they are on screen. The treatment is saved first.
protocols.newProtocolHint: A new protocol starts empty. Points and a prescription are added by applying it to a treatment and saving from there — that is where the point editor and the body chart are.
protocols.name: Name
protocols.indicationsHint: The pattern or complaint. This is what it is searched by.
protocols.empty: The usual way to make one is to finish a treatment and press "Save as protocol".

assistant.title: Ask about the data
assistant.subtitle: A question about the clinic’s numbers — how many, who, when. Not a clinical tool: what to prescribe is what the record is for.
assistant.placeholder: For example: how many new patients in the last six months?
assistant.privacyBody: The question and its results (names, dates and numbers) are sent to Anthropic to phrase the answer. Clinical records, ID numbers and addresses are never sent.
assistant.notConfigured: The assistant is not switched on yet
assistant.notConfiguredBody: It is switched on during installation, by whoever set the system up — the instructions are in the setup guide in the project folder. Everything else works as usual meanwhile.
assistant.unavailable: Could not reach the service. Try again in a moment.
assistant.gaveUp: I could not answer that from the data I can reach. Try putting it another way.
assistant.tooLong: That question is too long. One sentence is enough.

examples.inactive: Who has not been in for three months?
examples.herbs: Which herbs do I use most?

reports.title: Reports
reports.subtitle: The practice from a distance. The same numbers the assistant answers with, laid out at once.

reports.newVsReturningHint: How many treatments were a patient’s first, against returns.
reports.appointmentOutcomesHint: Cancellations and no-shows as a share of all bookings in the period.
reports.weekdayLoad: Load by day of the week
reports.topHerbsHint: By how often they were dispensed, not by weight.
reports.inactivePatientsHint: Patients with no treatment in the last three months.
reports.stockFine: No herb is below its threshold.

confirmations.title: Treatment confirmation
confirmations.subtitle: The document a patient submits to their health fund to claim. Tick the dates from the record, and add by hand any treatment that predates this system.
confirmations.noTreatments: No treatments recorded for this patient yet.
confirmations.addByHandHint: For treatment given before this system was in use.
confirmations.purposeHint: For example: for submission to Maccabi. Optional.
confirmations.selectedCount: {count, plural, =0 {No dates selected} one {1 date} other {# dates}}
confirmations.missingPractitioner: Fill in your name in the personal area before issuing a confirmation.

document.heading: Confirmation of treatment
document.statement: I, the undersigned, {practitioner}, ID {practitionerId}, hereby confirm that I treated {patient}, ID {patientId}, on the dates listed below.
document.datesHeading: {count, plural, one {Date of treatment} other {Dates of treatment (#)}}
document.disclaimer: A supporting document for an insurance claim. It is not a receipt and not a tax document. A receipt is issued separately.
